title: Deciphering the genomics of gene network regulation of T cell and fibroblast states in autoimmune inflammation
text:
NO CHANGE FROM ORIGINAL SUBMISSION
Narrative
We will develop advanced machine learning approaches to combine single-cell multiomic and bulk 3D
interactome data to model the impact of genetic variation on gene regulation, using rheumatoid arthritis (RA) as
a disease model. Our gene regulatory models and experimental analyses will focus on two cell types that drive
RA tissue pathology—T cells and synovial fibroblasts—and will serve as a case study for examining the genetics
of polygenic human diseases that dysregulate multiple interacting cell types within affected tissues.

title: Medical Marijuana, Emerging Adults, and Community: Connecting Health and Policy
text:
The proposed research is relevant to both public health and NIH’s mission because developing a clear
understanding of rules of controlled use of cannabis may lead to the policies and interventions that support safer
use of cannabis in policy environments where cannabis is increasingly accessible and potent.

title: Modernization of the Shielded Laminar Flow Environment for Molecular Probe Manufacture
text:
This application requests funds to purchase a modern Shielded Laminar Flow Hood to support
the manufacturing of investigational radiopharmaceuticals and other molecular imaging agents
intended for clinical research. Molecular imaging agents prepared using this equipment with either
be used to detect disease and measure response to therapies in human beings either non-
invasively or for use in image-guided surgery.

title: Physical Activity and Neurobehavioral Recovery in Pediatric TBI
text:
Physical activity has the potential to meet the critical need for evidence-based therapies that promote
neurobehavior in children with traumatic brain injury (TBI) by increasing expression of brain-derived
neurotrophic factor (BDNF). Despite promising evidence in similar populations, we currently know little about
physical activity after injury in these children; and families and healthcare providers often limit physical activity
for fear of exacerbating symptoms, which can have detrimental effects on TBI recovery. Using innovative multi-
disciplinary approaches, we will inform the development of an evidence-based, physical activity intervention to
improve neurobehavior in children with TBI by: (1) characterizing physical activity in the critical first six months
after TBI, (2) establishing the relationship between physical activity, BDNF and neurobehavior, and (3) co-
designing a physical activity intervention and testing the preliminary feasibility of this intervention in children
with TBI.

title: Cell-type-specific and spatial proteogenomics analysis of aberrant RNA splicing and misfolded proteins in Alzheimer's related tauopathies
text:
The proposed research will use cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics and proteogenomics platforms to map
molecular mechanisms underlying the dysregulation of aberrantly spliced and mis-processed proteins in AD
impacted brain regions. Our research will meet the major goals of RFA-AG-25-017 and facilitate the
development of better early diagnostic tools and new treatment strategies may be effective in preventing or
slowing AD/ADRD progression.

title: Sorting and Sequencing Latent Reservoirs in HIV+ Opioid Users
text:
The proposed research is responsive to RFA-DA-22-040 “High Priority HIV and Substance Use Research” and
is relevant to public health because it will apply cutting-edge technologies to identify, isolate and characterize
latently infected cells from people living with HIV who use opioids, with the goal of advancing new HIV-directed
cure strategies. This project supports the NIH’s mission and aligns with one of its high-priority topics of research
that awards AIDS-designated funds to support research toward a cure for HIV.

title: Using Forward Genetics to Explore the Genetics and Mechanisms of Early Onset Glaucoma
text:
While a large proportion of early-onset glaucoma cases have a genetic basis, only 12 genes have been
described so far for primary forms of the disease, compared to hundreds for retinal dystrophies. We have
recently shown that a powerful and unbiased state-of-the-science Forward Genetics approach can be
used to identify novel gene-phenotype associations that are crucial to retinal health, and we propose now
to exploit this strategy to identify and characterize genes, and pathways involved in the development of
early-onset glaucoma. Our long-term goal is to leverage research results from our Forward Genetics
studies to develop better clinical screening tests for genes associated with early-onset glaucoma, and to
discover novel diagnostic and therapeutic targets.

title: Developing multiparametric fluorescence microscopy to connect metabolism with cellular manipulations
text:
The overall goal of this project is to develop an innovative, sensitive, specific, and more accessible spatial
method to correlate metabolic changes associated with cellular manipulations. We propose combining multiple
phasor approaches - the phasor approach to Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging (phasor-FLIM, for metabolic
imaging), phasor approach to hyperspectral imaging (sp-phasor, protein expression/ membrane fluidity) and
phasor approach to Fluorescence Correlation Spectroscopy (phasor-FCS, protein diffusion). This method will
allow us to connect changes in one dimension (e.g., protein diffusion) to the changes in another (e.g.,
metabolism) in a pixel-wise manner.

title: Functional Genomics of LINE-1 Retrotransposition
text:
Taking advantage of technologies in functional genomics, studies are proposed in this
application to resolve molecular interactions between environmental carcinogens and
LINE-1 (Long Interspersed Element-1) retrotransposons in lung epithelial cells. LINE-1
is polymorphic in human populations and these variations may account for differences
in susceptibility to changes in oncogenic signaling, chromatin structure and malignant
transformation caused by LINE-1.

title: Comprehensive Cancer Center Support Grant
text:
The O'Neal Comprehensive Cancer Center is committed to reducing the cancer burdens and cancer disparities
in the State of Alabama. This is done through a basic science and population science strategic research plan
that is developed with community engagement and focused on elucidating the risk factors and mechanistic
underpinnings of these cancer burdens and cancer disparities. The results of this work are then translated
through diagnostic and therapeutic clinical trials to impact cancer outcomes and behavioral interventions to
mitigate cancer risks and improve the quality of life of cancer survivors in our catchment area.

title: Overcoming Acquired Resistance to BRAF Inhibition in Anaplastic Thyroid Cancer
text:
Project 1
Poorly differentiated (PDTC) and anaplastic thyroid cancers (ATC) are among the most aggressive solid tumors
seen in patients, with a mortality rate of almost 100% and a median overall survival of only 3-5 months. Recent
therapies with kinase inhibitors, such as a combination of dabrafenib and trametinib, have greatly increased
patient survival (up to 2-3 years). However, drug resistance always occurs, and all patients die early from the
disease; therefore, our overall objectives are 1) to understand the mechanisms of resistance to kinase therapies
and 2) to validate novel, safe and curative therapeutic interventions.

title: Wearable Sensor System for Continuous Monitoring of Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome
text:
Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome (AWS) is a life-threatening complication of Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD)
that is frequently underdiagnosed in outpatient settings, leading to preventable hospitalizations, complications,
and death. This project will develop a wearable sensor system that continuously monitors AWS severity using
physiological and biochemical signals, enabling earlier detection and treatment. By providing objective, real-time
assessment of withdrawal symptoms, this innovation has the potential to enhance outpatient care, reduce
healthcare costs, and improve outcomes for individuals with AUD.

title: Exploring and Exploiting Trehalose Metabolism in Rifampicin-Resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis
text:
Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health threat, and the incidence of rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium
tuberculosis (Mtb) complicates treatment and control efforts. This proposal seeks to understand metabolic
vulnerabilities in rifampicin-resistant Mtb, particularly within trehalose metabolism, which could inform the
development of targeted therapies to enhance treatment efficacy. Ultimately, these findings have the potential to
improve outcomes for drug-resistant TB cases and slow the emergence of resistance.

title: Revealing the transcriptional basis of corticothalamic projections using in situ sequence-based neuroanatomy
text:
Long-range projections of neuronal types underlie the structure of neuronal circuits and constrain
computations, but these relationship between projections and neuronal types remain largely unclear. We will
unravel the relationship between gene expression and projections in the mouse corticothalamic circuit by
combining state-of-the-art high-throughput in situ sequencing-based neuroanatomical techniques and robust
meta-analysis. We will build a comprehensive spatiotemporal map of the corticothalamic projections in the
context of neuronal gene expression and link our data with rich external reference single-cell RNAseq data to
extract gene-projection relationship with unprecedented details.

title: Massively Parallel Biochemical Annotation of Missense DNA Variants to Support Newborn Screening by Whole Genome Sequencing
text:
There is growing interest in whole genome sequencing of newborn genomes as a way to expand NBS to
include hundreds of pediatric and actionable diseases (newborn sequencing, NBSeq). In order to reduce false
negatives due to variants of unknown significance (VOUS), we will develop two massively parallel, rapid, and
inexpensive methods to biochemical annotate the degree of misfolding and degradation of all versions of a
protein in which each amino acid is substituted by all possible 19 other amino acids at one substitution per
protein.

title: Virulence of Staphylococcus aureus Corneal Infections
text:
Bacterial corneal infections (keratitis) caused by the bacteria Staphylococcus aureus often result in devastating,
vision-threatening complications and significantly contributes to the burden of world blindness. Currently our
ability to adequately treat this disease is limited by the lack of understanding of how S. aureus initiates and
maintains infection in this unique biologic niche. This project addresses this knowledge gap through a novel,
comprehensive approach for the identification and validation of the key bacterial drivers of S. aureus keratitis.

title: Topological Machine Learning to Characterize Higher-Order Brain Connectivity Alterations in Alzheimer's Disease
text:
Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is one of the most pressing health concerns that impacts over 55 million individuals
globally and non-invasive imaging biomarkers are being developed to discern the progression of disease. This
project aims to use innovative topological data analysis (TDA) and machine learning of functional and structural
brain connectomes derived from neuroimaging data for AD diagnostic classification. The successful completion
of this study will develop a novel set of non-invasive, network-based biomarkers for early detection and prediction
of Alzheimer’s disease using new machine learning paradigms.

title: Gene-environment interaction in islet serotonin metabolism and impacts on maternal glucose homeostasis
text:
The proposed application will use the mouse model to investigate how exposure to perfluorooctanoic acid
(PFOA) adversely influences maternal glucose homeostasis during pregnancy. Human studies suggest that
PFOA exposure is associated with increased risk for gestational diabetes, however these observations have
not been validated experimentally and the underlying mechanisms are not well understood. In this work, we will
define how exposure to PFOA disrupts serotonin metabolism in maternal pancreatic islets and how genetic
differences in vitamin B6 metabolism modulate the susceptibility to PFOA-induced gestational diabetes in
pregnant mice.

title: Novel Non-Contrast MRI to Assess Synovitis in Osteoarthritis
text:
Synovial inflammation (synovitis) plays a role in the onset, pathogenesis and is a key target for disease modifying
drugs in Osteoarthritis (OA), a leading cause of pain, reduced joint function, and disability. While associations
between synovitis and OA are known, our understanding of the role of synovitis in OA has been hampered by a
lack of a non-invasive and non-contrast methods to evaluate synovitis. This work aims to develop new, non-
contrast MRI methods to assess synovial inflammation in knee OA and to demonstrate their predictive power for
OA whole joint disease progression and both prediction and monitoring of treatment response.

title: Effectiveness Trial to Support Adoption of Hybrid Closed Loop Therapy in Underserved Adults with Type 1 Diabetes: Impact of System Functionality and Features on Lived Experience
text: We plan to conduct an effectiveness trial to evaluate the benefits and barriers to hybrid closed loop (HCL) pump therapy in adults with type 1 diabetes from lower income communities, and to apply the learnings to develop an implementation toolkit to support broader adoption of HCL in primary care.
